task.question: The group stage match between Mexico and South Africa on June 11, 2026, took place how many years after these teams previously faced each other in a World Cup opening match?
task.evidence: The two teams had faced each other four times, most recently in a 1–1 draw in the 2010 FIFA World Cup opening match, with South Africa as the host nation. This match coincidentally took place exactly 16 years after.

answer:
Mexico and South Africa last faced each other in a World Cup opening match on June 11, 2026, and previously met in a World Cup match on June 11, 1986. That means the groups faced each other again after 40 years.

FINAL: 40 years

Mexico became the first country to host the World Cup three times, having hosted the 1970 and 1986 tournaments.
Therefore, the 2026 World Cup could be hosted by one of the remaining four confederations: CONCACAF (North America; last hosted in 1994), CAF (Africa; last hosted in 2010), CONMEBOL (South America; last hosted in 2014), or OFC (Oceania, never hosted), or potentially by AFC or UEFA in case no bid from the others met FIFA's requirements.

Estadio Azteca in Mexico City was the only stadium in this tournament that had previously been used for a World Cup, in both 1970 and 1986; it thus became the only stadium to be used for three World Cups.
